correctness.rationale: The assumptions define a stable-focus coexistence equilibrium J=[[-alpha,-a n],[a b p,0]] with discriminant alpha^2<4d and n=m/(ab), p=(r/a)(1-n/K), d=rm(1-n/K). Exponential stability plus variation-of-constants establishes uniformly in time an O(epsilon^2) remainder for all bounded forcing inputs. For each frozen eta the first-order prey step response is epsilon s c exp(-alpha t/2) sin(qt)/q; |sin qt|<=qt bounds its maximum by 2 epsilon s c/(e alpha). Predator L1 convolution bound is epsilon s kappa coth(pi alpha/(4q)); strict u,v inequalities keep all frozen trajectories safely in coexistence for small epsilon. Periodic sine forcing at sqrt(d) has asymptotic prey amplitude epsilon s c/alpha, strictly exceeding the moving prey-barrier u epsilon, while its predator remains above the moving predator barrier. Crossing f1 into N<Na with P>Pa has an admissible Filippov f2 continuation with negative prey drift; subsequent prey extinction and eventually predator decay follow by differential inequalities. Exact step amplitude tends to ratio 2/e as q/alpha tends to 0, establishing sharpness of the universal sufficient comparison (not the full nonlinear tipping threshold).

value.rationale: PASS: a model-specific counterexample to frozen-parameter safety inference is conceptually meaningful, especially the explicit nonempty universal corridor and rigorous Filippov extinction despite asymptotically vanishing periodic forcing. The result separates oscillatory resonance from every constant-rate response using a sharp universal coefficient; it does not exaggerate into a full tipping phase diagram.

limitations: Only strictly co-moving thresholds and stable-focus parameter regimes are covered; finite-amplitude exact tipping boundaries are not determined.
A verifier output marker is corroboration only; the all-epsilon statement rests on the uniform nonlinear perturbation estimates and crossing inequalities.
